reading.body:
SV1 is a 82,850 sq ft facility in San Jose operated by Equinix as part of a 12-building Silicon Valley metro cluster serving over 10,500 customers. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building, making its power envelope opaque to public assessment. N+1 power redundancy and N+2 cooling redundancy qualify it for mission-critical colocation workloads that cannot tolerate downtime.

Without published power capacity, SV1's potential to host AI compute cannot be directly assessed. The facility is one of 103 mapped data centers in California but ranks outside the top 11 by published megawatts, indicating either smaller capacity than disclosed peers or deliberate non-disclosure. In a state holding 365 MW of published data center capacity, this building's actual contribution to AI infrastructure remains unknown.

The absence of a power specification from Equinix's own page for a retail colocation facility suggests either that capacity is allocated per-tenant under service agreements rather than published in aggregate, or that SV1 operates within broader campus power budgets not broken out by building. For readers evaluating where AI scaling can expand in Silicon Valley, SV1 cannot be ranked against other sites without that figure.
